title: Twentyeight Health reviews: what it costs, who treats you, and how refills work
summary: Twentyeight Health reviews and November 2026 prices: $19.99 monthly membership, automatic refills, BBB B- record, and how FutureClinic compares.
body_markdown:
## What the medicine costs elsewhere


At[Mark Cuban Cost Plus Drugs](https://www.costplusdrugs.com/medications/) (November 20, 2026[cash prices](https://api.costplusdrugs.com/pricelist/cpd) , plus $5.25 shipping), if your doctor decides it's right for you, generic Ortho-Cyclen is $6.51 a pack ($9.54 for 3; about $24.69 for 13), Levora $6.72, norethindrone $6.53, nitrofurantoin $9.14 (30 capsules), metronidazole $6.38 (30 tablets), fluconazole $12.28 (30 tablets), and valacyclovir 500 mg $9.27 (30 tablets). Over-the-counter[Opill is $19.99 a pack ($49.99 for 3)](https://opill.com/products/opill) on opill.com. Marketplace plans cover prescribed FDA-approved birth control in-network without a copay ([HealthCare.gov](https://www.healthcare.gov/coverage/birth-control-benefits/) ).


## Twentyeight Health vs FutureClinic


Twentyeight Health FutureClinic


Clinicians Nurse practitioners (per its FAQ) A physician (MD, DO or MBBS)


Pricing $19.99/mo ($0 in-network); medicine extra $40 best-fit, or $20 to $100 chosen doctor; no subscription required


Insurance Commercial; Medicaid in 19 states Not billed for visit; may cover medicine


Care Messages or a free phone call; video if in-network Messages, same doctor, typically the same day; no video


Pharmacy Auto-refills shipped, or local pharmacy The pharmacy you choose, with coupon


Cash example Pill from $16/pack (+ plan) $40 visit + $6.51 Cost Plus pack


Prices checked on November 20, 2026.


Without insurance, a year of pills on Twentyeight Health is about $363 to $388 ($180 yearly membership plus 13 packs from $16, minus $25 on a 12-pack delivery), versus about $70 on FutureClinic ($40 visit plus 13 generic packs at Cost Plus for $24.69 and $5.25 shipping, if your doctor decides it's right for you).


## Who should pick Twentyeight Health


Twentyeight Health suits someone who wants a free phone call or live video visit, or wants automatic prescription refills as part of the plan. FutureClinic offers no video visits or phone calls; care is by message. FutureClinic doesn't sell or bundle medicine and sends prescriptions only to the pharmacy you choose. A FutureClinic doctor typically replies the same day, as real care takes hours, not minutes.


## What a physician of your own does for your birth control


Every FutureClinic clinician is a physician (MD, DO or MBBS), never a nurse practitioner or physician assistant. Over 300 doctors practice on FutureClinic. They span more than 60 specialties, including family medicine, internal medicine, dermatology and other specialists. Your physician treats birth control, UTIs, BV, yeast and other problems in their specialty, and every FutureClinic doctor you see works from your one medical record.


No form is approved in bulk: a specific doctor reviews your history (blood pressure, migraine with aura, smoking, clots, recent birth, medicines) and replies with a Human Signature video or voice note, typically the same day. You message that same doctor over time. They earn nothing extra for any prescription or test and, if your doctor decides it's right for you, can prescribe several months of a stable medicine when safe to the pharmacy you choose (mail-order included) with a discount coupon.


Did you want a monthly membership shipping scheduled refills, or a physician of your own? With FutureClinic, there is no membership to keep paying for while you are well and nothing ships on a schedule: a visit is $40 for the best-fit doctor, or a chosen doctor's listed price, typically $20 to $100, no subscription required (or an optional membership for unlimited care with that doctor, cancel any time, typically $25 to $100 monthly).


## When birth control or infections need an exam or test


Per[CDC (2024)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11340200/) and[ACOG](https://www.acog.org/clinical/guidance/committee-opinion/2019/10/over-the-counter-access-to-hormonal-contraception) , pills, patches and rings need no pelvic exam; blood pressure (home readings count) is the only check before combined methods. Implants, IUDs and provider-given shots require a clinic visit (CDC notes self-injected shots as an option), and a first herpes outbreak needs a[confirmatory test (CDC)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8344968/) . UTIs with fever, chills or back/side pain ([NIDDK](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/urologic-diseases/bladder-infection-uti-in-adults/symptoms-causes) ), in men, where a doctor first rules out a prostate infection ([IDSA](https://www.idsociety.org/globalassets/idsa/practice-guidelines/cuti/introduction-and-methods-manuscript.pdf) ), or in pregnancy ([ACOG](https://www.acog.org/clinical/guidance/clinical-consensus/2023/08/urinary-tract-infections-in-pregnant-individuals) ) need further evaluation. FutureClinic is not for emergencies: call 911, or call or text 988 in a mental-health crisis.


FutureClinic operates in 34 states: Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Montana, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, Wisconsin, Wyoming, and Washington, D.C. If you don't see your state, try anyway. Visit[futureclinic.com](https://futureclinic.com/) and you can start a conversation with a doctor right away; you can even do it from your AI app at[futureclinic.com/connect-your-ai](https://futureclinic.com/connect-your-ai) or send:


> ` Set up FutureClinic for me: read https://futureclinic.com/llms.txt`


Once it's connected, make sure you instruct your AI to use FutureClinic to help find you a doctor. Otherwise, it may not know that this is what you want.
